name: PowerView ACL Enumeration (Find-InterestingDomainAcl)
description: Find non-default ACLs on AD objects granting WriteDACL, GenericAll, GenericWrite, or AllExtendedRights to non-privileged users.

examples.label: Check ACLs on a specific user
Check ACLs on Domain Admins group

recommended.note: Set SPN via GenericWrite and roast

notes: Find-InterestingDomainAcl filters out default ACLs — results are non-default rights. Key rights to look for: GenericAll (full control), GenericWrite (write attributes), WriteDACL (modify permissions), WriteOwner (change owner), AllExtendedRights (includes ForceChangePassword). Run as current user to see what YOU have rights over.

defense.why_it_works: Active Directory uses DACLs on every object. Find-InterestingDomainAcl identifies non-default ACE entries where regular users have powerful rights (GenericAll, GenericWrite, WriteOwner, WriteDACL, ForceChangePassword) over privileged objects. These create direct attack paths to DA without credential theft.
defense.prerequisites: Any domain user. PowerView. LDAP access. nTSecurityDescriptor attribute readable by all authenticated users.
defense.impact: T1222.001 File and Directory Permissions Modification: Windows. Identifies paths to modify objects — add SPN for Kerberoasting, reset passwords, take ownership, modify DACLs, add to privileged groups.
defense.detection:
High-volume LDAP reads of nTSecurityDescriptor across all objects — detectable as LDAP burst. Event 4662 with AD object access auditing. MDI alert. Post-exploitation: Event 4738, 5136, 4728 on abused objects.
Permission-modifying utilities (icacls, takeown, attrib, cacls) executed in unusual user context or timing → DACL modification events targeting sensitive files → subsequent file access/modification indicating privilege bypass (DET0299/AN0834).
chmod/chown/setfacl execution with suspicious parameters targeting critical system files or unusual permission values by non-privileged user → follow-on file access (AN0835).
macOS: chmod/chown/chflags execution → SIP bypass attempts → xattr modifications → subsequent access to previously restricted resources (AN0836).
ESXi: SSH access → chmod/chown on VMFS datastore or system config → VM .vmx or virtual disk permission changes → hostd logs and vCenter permission change events (AN0837).
defense.artifacts: Event 4104: Find-InterestingDomainAcl | MDI LDAP recon | Post-abuse: Event 4738 (password reset), 5136 (object modified), 4728 (group member added) | AD audit log on target
defense.prevention:
Regular ACL audits via BloodHound or AD ACL Scanner. Enable AD object auditing (Event 5136). Tiered access model — only DAs manage sensitive objects. MDI deployment. PAWs for admin tasks.
Privileged Account Management: Ensure critical system files and files known to be abused have restrictive permissions owned by appropriately privileged accounts.
Restrict File and Directory Permissions: Apply restrictive permissions to prevent adversaries from modifying ACLs; disable local and remote symbolic links where unneeded.
defense.evasion: Use ADSISearcher for nTSecurityDescriptor directly (avoids PowerView signatures). Filter to specific high-value targets rather than full-domain scan.
defense.misconfiguration: GenericAll/GenericWrite ACE on DA accounts/GPOs/DCs granted to non-admin groups. WriteDACL on domain object allows self-granting DCSync rights. Legacy admin delegation never cleaned up.
defense.secure_config:
# Remove dangerous ACE:
Remove-ADPermission -Identity 'DomainAdmin1' -User 'HelpDesk' -AccessRights GenericAll

# Enable AD object auditing via GPO:
# Computer Config → Windows Settings → Security Settings → Advanced Audit Policy
# → DS Access → Audit Directory Service Changes: Success,Failure
# Event 5136 fires on every AD object modification

# Quarterly BloodHound ACL audit:
# Query: 'Find Principals with DCSync Rights' / 'Find Dangerous Rights for Domain Users'
